ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the directly proportional function $y=-x$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y=kx+ \frac{5}{2}$ (where $k\neq 0$) at point $P$. What is the solution to the equation $-x=kx+ \frac{5}{2}$ in terms of $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the coordinates of point P be $(x, 1)$,\\
Substituting $(x, 1)$ into $y=-x$,\\
$\therefore$ $-x=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $x=-1$,\\
Thus, the coordinates of point P are $(-1, 1)$,\\
$\therefore$ the solution to the equation concerning $x$, $-x=kx+ \frac{5}{2}$, is $x=\boxed{-1}$.
